## Declaration 1 — Naming Correction: "The CDS Threshold"

### Revoked Name
**"External Threshold Gate"** — used throughout documents 0210, 0220, 0200, 0070, and the CSPS-CL series.

### Approved Name
**"The CDS Threshold"**

### Why This Change
The name "External Threshold Gate" was produced before CDS and CSE were named. The gate is the physical implementation of the CDS vision — the mechanism that makes CSE possible. Its name must reflect its role in the CDS/CSE/CSPS architecture.

### Everywhere "External Threshold Gate" Appears — Replace With

| Context | Old Text | New Text |
|---|---|---|
| Document references | "External Threshold Gate (0220)" | "The CDS Threshold (0220)" |
| Sprint deliverables (0070) | "Build External Threshold Gate" | "Build The CDS Threshold" |
| Build Initiation Protocol (0200) | "External Threshold Gate (0220) will not open" | "The CDS Threshold (0220) will not open" |
| ICE specification (0210) | "External Threshold Gate interface" | "The CDS Threshold interface" |
| All other references | "External Threshold Gate" | "The CDS Threshold" |

### Backward Propagation Targets
- 0200 — Platform Build Initiation Protocol
- 0210 — Intake Classification Engine
- 0220 — The CDS Threshold (document title updated)
- 0070 — Corespiral Implementation Protocol
- 0150 — Swift Implementation Protocol

## Declaration 2 — CDS and CSE References — Suite-Wide Injection

The following terms are now formally declared in the CSPS vocabulary (CS-GOV-003) and apply across all 53 documents:

### New Vocabulary Entries

**CDS — Core Driven Solutions**
- CORE: The next generation platform. Built by the CSPS engine. Standalone, sovereign, separate. An improved second generation that inherits lessons — not code.
- MEDIUM: CDS does not replace CSPS. Both are sovereign. Both are governed. CDS emerges from CSPS's constitutional architecture applied to a new context. Good: distinct identity, own constitutional layer, own ratification ceremonies. Bad: treating CDS as a CSPS extension or fork.
- FULL: CDS is the proof that the governing principles generalise. Every gap CDS exposes in the inherited architecture travels back through CSE — improving CSPS. This is why generation-to-generation relationships matter: the next generation is the most rigorous test of the previous generation's principles.

**CSE — Core Symbiosis Engine**
- CORE: The collaborative process engine built by CSPS that enables sovereign platforms to share, consult, debate, reach conclusions, and evolve — without merging or losing governed identity.
- MEDIUM: CSE has five components: The Playground, Versioning System, The CDS Threshold, Universal Insight Archive, Multi-Participant Architecture. The process inside CSE: Share → Consult → Debate → Conclusions → Each platform adapts → Universal insights archived → Each platform proceeds independently. Good: sovereignty preserved at every step, vocabulary alignment before any exchange, versioned outputs per participant. Bad: shared ownership of conclusions, treating CSE output as binding rather than informing.
- FULL: CSE is what makes generation-to-generation evolution governed rather than arbitrary. Without CSE, knowledge produced by one generation is lost or corrupted in transmission. With CSE, wisdom propagates through a governed gate — aligned, optimised, and adapted before absorption. CSE is the intelligence infrastructure for the CDS family of platforms.

**The CDS Threshold**
- CORE: The gate mechanism — the only door through which inputs enter the platform. Classifies, aligns vocabulary, injects platform DNA, and routes every input before any platform mechanism processes it.
- MEDIUM: The CDS Threshold enforces six rules mechanically — all server-side, none bypassable. It processes five source types: human user, developer, external AI, tenant API, internal agent. Good: standalone external page — not a frame inside the platform. The gate is the only door. Bad: treating The CDS Threshold as a UI component rather than a constitutional enforcement mechanism.
- FULL: The CDS Threshold is the reason CSE is possible. Without a governed gate on each side of an exchange, shared intelligence is contamination. The Threshold is not just an input classifier — it is the mechanism that makes the platform's sovereignty real at the boundary.

**The Playground**
- CORE: A sandboxed space inside CSE where participating platforms meet, share, consult, and debate. Nothing in the Playground is engraved in any platform until consensus is formally declared.
- MEDIUM: The Playground is owned by CSE — not by any participant. It is neutral ground managed by the CSE Orchestrator. Good: all participants enter with equal standing, conclusions are versioned per participant before distribution, no platform is obligated by what others decide to do with conclusions. Bad: treating Playground conclusions as binding, allowing un-gated content to enter the Playground.
- FULL: The Playground is the structural answer to the question of how sovereign platforms learn from each other without losing sovereignty. It is the place where "nothing stands alone" applies to platforms themselves — each platform is connected to others through this space, but remains distinct and governed in its own right.

**Universal Insight Archive**
- CORE: The repository of insights that all CSE participants agree are universally true — not owned by any platform, queryable by all, absorbed through each platform's own gate.
- MEDIUM: Universal insights are promoted through the same process as Intelligence Vault entries: evidence accumulation, confidence level progression, Governor-equivalent approval. Good: insights clearly tagged with contributing platforms and consensus date, each platform absorbs through its own vocabulary alignment layer. Bad: treating archived insights as prescriptive rather than informing.
- FULL: The Universal Insight Archive is what survives individual platforms. CSPS and CDS will both evolve and eventually be superseded. The wisdom they produce — if correctly archived — serves every generation that comes after them. This is the long game: not building better platforms, but building the infrastructure through which platforms teach each other to be better.
